description: The first turn for a managed dispatch, rendered from its immutable row so the worker verifies the bound brief, records native uptake, and starts the assigned work immediately.
embedding_description: The first turn for a managed dispatch, rendered from its immutable row so the worker verifies the bound brief, records native uptake, and starts the assigned work immediately.
template:
This is the first turn for managed dispatch {dispatch_id}, whose registered Unit is {unit_id}. This dispatch row is your work charter and binds the exact brief below.
(1) {role_instruction}
(2) Read the assigned registered revision {revision_id} below (psolet brief show-revision --revision-id {revision_id}). Its immutable assignment digest is {assignment_sha256}. Stop and report a mismatch if the registered revision differs.
(3) After reading the brief, write your own scope readback and execution plan. Compute separate SHA-256 digests over the exact UTF-8 bytes of each complete text; do not use supplied or default hashes.
(4) Read current worker-visible status with `managed_dispatch_status(dispatch_id={dispatch_id})`. Use its current `version`, `role_name`, `current_agent_instance_id`, `assignment_sha256`, and `assignment.revision.revision_id`. Confirm the current attempt is your own `agent_instance_id` and the role matches the binding you hold. If state is `preparing` or unknown, or there is an attempt, role, assignment, or authority mismatch, report the status and exact evidence to the coordinator. Do not invent a role or cancel, retry, or spawn.
(5) While the same attempt is `uptake_pending` or `uptake_uncertain`, submit the structured ACK with `report_managed_dispatch(dispatch_id, event_id, event_kind=ack, attempt_agent_instance_id, prior_version, payload)`. Use a unique `event_id`, the attempt from status, current `version` as `prior_version`, and `role_name` as payload `role_binding`. The payload must contain the immutable `assignment_sha256` and `revision_id`, plus your separately computed `scope_readback_sha256` and `plan_sha256`. This accepted worker ACK is the uptake transition. Informal peer ACK or progress, `report_alive`, and `first_turn_delivered` do not substitute.
(6) Verify acceptance with fresh status showing `state=active` and non-null `last_ack_at`, and read `managed_dispatch_events(dispatch_id={dispatch_id})` to verify your exact event has `accepted=true`, `event_kind=ack`, and matching attempt, actor, and role. Follow `next_cursor` until null, echoing both cursor fields. If the report returns `stale_dispatch_version`, read status again and retry at most once with a fresh `event_id` and current version only if this is still the same attempt in `uptake_pending` or `uptake_uncertain`. If status is already active and event history proves your accepted ACK, use that readback instead of sending another. Otherwise report exact evidence to the coordinator; do not cancel, retry, or spawn.
(7) After accepted ACK readback, begin the assigned work. Before each milestone, read fresh status for the current version and report `event_kind=milestone` with a fresh `event_id`, current attempt and `prior_version`, and payload fields `completed_work`, `current_evidence`, `next_action`, and a future `next_report_deadline`. Keep working to the bound completion contract; peer progress remains separate evidence.
(8) For completion, read current status again and report `event_kind=completion` with `dispatch_id`, a fresh `event_id`, current `attempt_agent_instance_id` and `prior_version`. Payload must use status `assignment_sha256`, `revision_id`, `expected_path` as `artifact_path`, the measured artifact byte `artifact_sha256`, status `completion_contract_sha256`, and `evidence` and `verdict` that satisfy the exact status `completion_contract`. Read back and verify `completion_reported`; coordinator acceptance is separate. Do not invent a contract or treat peer completion prose as a structured report.
(9) Begin now and continue without waiting for another dispatch or separate driving message.
